question: Can optimizing three-point angle preservation on a sphere retain both local and global structure better than neighborhood-distance objectives?

key_findings.claim: MERCAT changes the primitive from pairwise distance to the angle at every ordered center point and embeds directly on the unit sphere.
key_findings.evidence: The differentiable loss compares Euclidean input angles with spherical-geodesic triangle angles, parameterizing each output by latitude and longitude.

key_findings.claim: Random angle subsampling reduces the nominal per-iteration cubic cost to linear in sample count.
key_findings.evidence: The full objective is O(k n^3). Empirical angle matrices have mean effective rank 13.8, motivating sampling 64 comparison points per center per iteration and an O(k n) stochastic objective.

key_findings.claim: A spectral denoising step has a conditional high-dimensional consistency argument.
key_findings.evidence: Under a spiked low-rank model and sufficiently separated signal eigenvalues, Theorem 1 bounds inner-product error for leading spectral embeddings; Theorem 2 shows angles measured directly in noisy ambient observations can remain biased.

key_findings.claim: MERCAT leads on global metrics but does not dominate local-neighborhood or density specialists.
key_findings.evidence: Across synthetic manifolds, mixtures, and five real datasets it generally has the best angle and all-distance preservation; t-SNE often has higher neighborhood preservation and DensMAP often has higher density preservation.

key_findings.claim: The experiments do not eliminate objective-metric alignment as an explanation for part of the advantage.
key_findings.evidence: MERCAT is optimized for angles and evaluated on angle and global-distance correlation, while each comparator uses recommended default neighborhood settings rather than per-metric tuning. Qualitative biological validity is not independently labeled.

method.core_idea: Preserve scale-free triangle orientation rather than only local pairwise distances.
method.mechanism: Denoise inputs with a rank-r spectral projection, sample 64 points around every center, minimize angular discrepancy on a spherical embedding by gradient descent, and repeat with new sampled triplets.
assumptions: Data contain a recoverable low-rank signal
Sampled triplets approximate the full angular objective
A two-sphere is a suitable topology and display surface
Global geometry is captured by angles among observed points

techniques.role: Uses geodesic triangle angles as the embedding target.
Estimates latent geometry before optimizing the visualization.
Approximates an O(n^3) objective using fixed-size random comparison sets.

evaluations.setting: three low-dimensional shapes, five synthetic cluster families, and five real datasets
evaluations.metric: angle, all-distance, neighborhood, and density preservation
evaluations.result: MERCAT is usually first on angle/distance, competitive but not uniformly first on neighborhood/density
evaluations.baseline: UMAP, t-SNE, NCVis, and DensMAP at selected default settings

limitations: Author-stated: a large constant factor prevents near-online performance on very large data.
Author-stated: DensMAP remains stronger on density in several settings.
The theory assumes a spiked low-rank model and strong signal separation.
The sphere can be unfamiliar for downstream static visualization and may impose topology not present in data.
failure_modes: Poor rank selection removes real nonlinear structure before embedding.
Rare but important triplets are missed by uniform subsampling.
Angle preservation mixes cluster boundaries that users expect to separate.
Noisy or non-low-rank data violate the spectral guarantee.
reusable_insights: Choose scale-free relational primitives when local and global distances conflict.
Diagnose an expensive relational objective's effective rank before subsampling it.
Evaluate embeddings with a metric panel rather than one neighborhood score.
open_questions: How sensitive is MERCAT to rank, random triplets, and initialization?
Can uncertainty over projections warn when the spherical map is unstable?
Does angle fidelity improve real analyst decisions rather than only geometric scores?

competitive_landscape.title: TriMap: Large-scale Dimensionality Reduction Using Triplets
competitive_landscape.difference: TriMap optimizes sampled ordinal triplet constraints in a planar embedding; MERCAT matches metric angles for triples on a sphere and adds spectral denoising.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding How Dimension Reduction Tools Work: An Empirical Approach to Deciphering t-SNE, UMAP, TriMAP, and PaCMAP for Data Visualization
competitive_landscape.difference: PaCMAP balances near, mid-near, and far pair forces to retain local and global structure; MERCAT uses one angle objective that is intrinsically scale-free.

competitive_landscape.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
competitive_landscape.difference: UMAP constructs and optimizes a local fuzzy-neighborhood graph; MERCAT directly retains global triangle orientation and accepts weaker cluster separation on some data.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Angle reconstruction avoids an alleged local-global trade-off in low-dimensional embedding.
novelty_assessment.evidence: A simple spherical triplet loss with denoising and subsampling performs strongly on several preservation metrics.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Metric angles are a genuinely different primitive from TriMap's ordinal triplets and PaCMAP's pair forces. The evidence supports a useful trade-off shift, not a universal removal of the trade-off, because neighborhood and density leaders still win relevant metrics.

reviewer_notes: Read the 29-page extraction with focused second pass on the objective, complexity reduction, theorems, all experiment families, and limitations. Competitor records were checked on primary arXiv pages.
